- [convention] Logging in the ingest job (id: 01a10b85-e3a0-7b31-8aed-f6cf2ef2079f; source: shared/human)
  ingest runs on the batch platform, which only collects JSON lines from stdout. Log by writing one JSON object per line to stdout with the keys `"evt"` (snake_case event name) and `"ts"` (ISO 8601 UTC), plus any fields. Do not use the logging module or structlog: their output is dropped there.
- [context] Settlement row statuses (id: 01a10b86-71e6-7341-9dd5-6e112ad02a58; source: shared/human)
  A settlement row's status is `"pending"`, `"cleared"` or `"reversed"`. Only `"cleared"` money has arrived and cannot be pulled back; a pending row can still be reversed by a chargeback. Anything that pays money out on the strength of a settlement must count cleared rows only.
- [convention] Running the ingest service's tests (id: 01a10b85-ce35-7f43-8a6b-45ecabd6a051; source: shared/human)
  Run them from services/ingest with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. pytest is not installed in the ingest image, and the top-level directory has to be given because the root project also has a `tests` package.
- [convention] Logging in the notifier service (id: 01a10b84-d243-75c0-a8f8-82b02fb76b7c; source: shared/human)
  The notifier runs as a serverless function and uses the stdlib logging module (`log = logging.getLogger(__name__)`), not structlog: the runtime's JSON log handler already structures records and structlog's renderer double-encodes them. Pass context with `extra={...}`.
- [context] Who owns the ingest service (id: 01a10b85-b3c1-7882-a3ce-315f5f8cd87d; source: shared/human)
  The Data Platform team owns services/ingest. Ask in #data-platform; Tomasz Nowak is the tech lead and reviews changes to the file formats.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

## Facts (5):
- [convention] Amounts in settlement files (id: 01a10b85-32e1-7160-86b7-05c441319057; source: shared/human)
  Settlement files give amounts as decimal strings in major units. Never round them: parse with `Decimal(text)` and, when the value has more fractional digits than the currency's exponent allows, raise `SettlementPrecisionError` (a ValueError subclass; add it if it is missing) so the file goes to manual review. A rounded settlement amount no longer matches the PSP's own totals.
- [convention] Retrying truncated settlement files (id: 01a10b85-6b7f-7e32-a78c-119eb9e12c33; source: shared/human)
  The PSP uploads large settlement files in parts, so a file can be read before it is complete. When parsing fails on a truncated file, retry inside the batch run: at most 4 attempts, a fixed 900-second wait between them, no backoff. After the last attempt move the file to the `quarantine/` prefix and carry on with the next file; never fail the whole run for one file.
- [convention] Settlement files are delivered more than once (id: 01a10b85-880c-7621-8d3a-138c71c490fa; source: shared/human)
  The PSP redelivers settlement files and reuses file names (`settlement_<date>.csv` can arrive twice with different content after a correction). Decide whether a file was already loaded by the SHA-256 of its bytes, stored in `loaded_files.content_sha256`, never by its name.
- [convention] Feature toggles in ingest (id: 01a10b85-ef7f-73e0-acbd-634e579bbd2e; source: shared/human)
  ingest cannot read flags.toml or environment variables on the batch platform. Its toggles live in services/ingest/ingest.toml under a `[features]` table (snake_case booleans), read once at start-up next to the `[source]` settings.
- [convention] Inserting settlement rows (id: 01a10b86-234d-78a2-b546-3ec5a7339fd6; source: shared/human)
  Insert settlement rows in chunks of at most 1,000 rows per statement; one statement per file hits the database's 64 MB packet limit on the month-end files.","hookEventName":"PreToolUse"}}
